perspective:
From Mason Hurley’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am an accountant at a small community center. Martha Moua is a colleague/personal care aide there; we interact professionally and are not personally close.
- I reviewed financial reports and noticed discrepancies: healthcare expenses seemed unusually high and did not match usual spending patterns. This made me suspicious and anxious that Martha might be mismanaging funds.
- I asked Martha to discuss the report. I told her the numbers didn’t add up and pointed to the healthcare expenses. She said there may have been a misentry and that she would review and correct errors.
- After reviewing with Martha, I understood the discrepancies were a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. I felt relieved and embarrassed. I thanked her, apologized for my initial suspicion, and said I should have asked her first. She said errors happen, I was being thorough, and suggested double-checking entries next time.
- I now believe Martha is competent. I think recurring clerical errors show the current financial management system is inadequate. I feel frustrated with the system and empathetic toward Martha.
- I told Martha the issue isn’t her management but the current system, and I proposed drafting a new, more robust financial system. She agreed and offered input.
- I drafted the proposal. I hope it will benefit operations, but I am uncertain whether management will approve or implement it. I told Martha this. She encouraged me to present confidently and said it was solid. I planned a detailed presentation and asked her to help gather data; she agreed.
- I presented the proposal to management. I think it went well. I feel satisfied but physically and mentally exhausted, and I believe I’ve done everything I can. Now it is up to management.
- Martha praised my work, suggested I take time off, and offered help while away. I plan to take a few days off to recharge and reflect, hoping for good news.
- I do not know management’s decision yet, nor Martha’s private thoughts or motives beyond what she said.
